title: Can India sustain its 19.7% China yarn share as disruptions fade?
content:
India’s cotton-yarn shipments to China rose roughly fivefold from November 2025 to about 1,500 containers, or 30,000 tonnes, a month.
Its share of China’s cotton-yarn imports reached 19.71 per cent in January–February 2026, overtaking Pakistan.
The share slipped to 17.71 per cent in April, behind Vietnam’s about 44 per cent, suggesting the surge may have peaked.

title: India targets wider FTA use to boost exports across 780 districts
content:
India has called for a nationwide FTA utilisation drive to turn trade agreements into export gains for MSMEs and first-time exporters. 
It will cover all 780 districts, targeting traders, startups and women entrepreneurs. 
Minister of Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal said nine FTAs span economies representing about $60 trillion in GDP and offer preferential access to nearly two-thirds of global trade.

title: US economic activity grows modestly as manufacturing picks up
content:
US economic activity grew modestly since early July, with 10 of 12 Fed Districts reporting slight to moderate expansion, as per the August Beige Book. 
Consumer spending rose slightly but remained price-sensitive, while manufacturing activity improved across most regions. 
Employment rose marginally, labour demand stayed strongest in manufacturing, and outlook remained positive despite uncertainty.

title: ICE cotton furthers decline sharply due to profit booking
content:
ICE cotton futures declined sharply amid heavy selling pressure and profit booking, with December 2026 settling at 88.93 cents per pound, down 2.62 cent. 
Trading volume rose to 107,487 contracts, while open interest reached 382,071 contracts on Tuesday, the third-highest level ever. 
Rising crude oil and the continuing US-Iran conflict added volatility across commodity markets.

title: Vietnam's yarn exports to China surge, may redraw Asia's yarn map
content:
Vietnam's textile and apparel exports are growing again in 2026, according to Vietnam Customs.
In January-July, fibre and yarn exports rose 11.34 per cent and fabric exports 9.57 per cent, while garment exports increased only 0.70 per cent.
Garments still account for about four-fifths of export value, but growth is increasingly coming from upstream materials.

title: US Kontoor Brands targets $1.1bn Helly Hansen revenue by 2030
content:
Kontoor Brands is targeting Helly Hansen revenue of more than $1.1 billion by 2030, with around 10 per cent CAGR from its 2025 base. 
The company also aims for gross margins in the mid- to high-50 per cent range, operating margins in the mid-teens and cumulative cash generation above $500 million, driven by US expansion, premium outdoor growth and North American workwear.

title: Why did US’ G-III Apparel’s Q2 profits surge despite lower sales?
content:
G-III Apparel Group raised its FY27 earnings guidance after Q2 net income more than doubled to $20.2 million, despite a 10 per cent sales decline to $554.1 million. 
Gross margin expanded 440 basis points to 45.2 per cent, while its go-forward portfolio grew at a high-single digit rate. 
The Marc Jacobs acquisition and improved margins support its growth outlook.

title: What drove US’ Tillys' Q1 FY26 sales & margin gains?
content:
Tillys reported a strong start to fiscal 2026, with Q1 net sales rising 15.9 per cent year on year to $124.7 million and comparable sales increasing 22.9 per cent. 
Gross margin expanded 910 basis points to 28.9 per cent, while the net loss narrowed to $8 million. 
The retailer expects Q2 sales growth of 6-10 per cent and remains focused on returning to full-year profitability.

title: $390 mn trade flow reveals India-Sri Lanka’s new apparel model
content:
TexPro data shows India and Sri Lanka increasingly acting as one production corridor, with India supplying inputs and Sri Lanka retaining an export-oriented garment base.
Sri Lanka imported $1.003 billion of fabric in H1 2026; India supplied 28.52 per cent, and 34.44 per cent of yarn.

title: Sea freight cuts T-shirt carbon footprint by up to 60%: Canada study
content:
Concordia-led research finds polyester T-shirts emit more greenhouse gases than cotton, while cotton has higher land and water demands. 
Air freight is a major emissions driver; switching to sea freight can cut a shirt's carbon footprint by roughly 30 to 60 per cent. 
Longer garment lifespans, fewer new items and durability-focused design offer supply-chain levers for fast-fashion supply chains.
